proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 1 and 2, i.e. the choice (31) of the integer β_F and the bound (35) in Simon's proof of the Deformation Theorem (Ch. 6, 5.1; chapter-06.txt). Notation: n := m + 1, Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}, Lⁿ := volume on Euclid n, μ := Lⁿ⌞Q₁ (volume.restrict Q₁).

0. Preliminaries.
 (a) Q₁ is open (a finite intersection of the open sets {y : 0 < y_i} and {y : y_i < 1}; the coordinate maps y ↦ y_i are continuous), hence Borel.
 (b) Lⁿ(Q₁) = 1. The coordinate map y ↦ (y_0, …, y_m) (WithLp.ofLp) is a measure-preserving bijection from Euclid n onto ℝ^{Fin n} with the product Lebesgue measure (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp; inverse PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp). It maps Q₁ onto the box ∏_i (0, 1) = Set.pi univ (fun _ => Ioo 0 1), whose measure is ∏_i (1 − 0) = 1 (Real.volume_pi_Ioo).
 (c) Measurable representative. u is integrable on Q₁, so it is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ. Fix a Borel function ũ with u = ũ μ-almost everywhere. The set Z := Q₁ ∩ {u ≠ ũ} is Lⁿ-null (Q₁ is measurable, so μ-null subsets of Q₁ are Lⁿ-null). Hence for every Borel set B ⊆ ℝ the sets Q₁ ∩ u⁻¹(B) and Q₁ ∩ ũ⁻¹(B) differ only inside Z. So Q₁ ∩ u⁻¹(B) is Lⁿ-null-measurable and has the same Lⁿ-measure as the Borel set Q₁ ∩ ũ⁻¹(B). This applies in particular to A_b := Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ b} and to Q₁ ∩ {b ≤ u}, for b ∈ ℝ.

1. The distribution function. For b ∈ ℤ put F(b) := Lⁿ(A_b) ∈ [0, 1]. F is nondecreasing, since A_b ⊆ A_{b'} for b ≤ b'.
 – F(N) → 1 as N → ∞ (N ∈ ℕ). Indeed, the sets A_N increase, and their union is Q₁ because u is real-valued. Continuity of measure from below (tendsto_measure_iUnion_atTop) gives F(N) → Lⁿ(Q₁) = 1. Since 1/2 < 1, there is N₁ ∈ ℕ with F(N₁) > 1/2.
 – F(−N) → 0 as N → ∞. The sets A_{−N} decrease, are null-measurable, have finite measure (≤ 1), and have empty intersection. Continuity from above (tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop) gives F(−N) → 0. Hence there is N₀ ∈ ℕ with F(−N₀) < 1/2. By monotonicity, F(b) < 1/2 for every integer b ≤ −N₀.

2. Choice of β (Simon (31)). The set S := {b ∈ ℤ : F(b) ≥ 1/2} contains N₁. Every element of S is > −N₀, so S is bounded below. Let β be its least element (Int.exists_least_of_bdd, or csInf_mem in ℤ). Then F(β) ≥ 1/2 and, as β − 1 ∉ S, F(β − 1) < 1/2.

3. Two-sided median property.
 – First, Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β}) = F(β) ≥ 1/2.
 – Second, u is integer-valued. So for every y, β ≤ u(y) holds iff u(y) ≤ β − 1 fails: if u(y) = z ∈ ℤ, then β ≤ z ⟺ ¬(z ≤ β − 1). Hence Q₁ ∩ {β ≤ u} = Q₁ ∖ A_{β−1}. The set A_{β−1} ⊆ Q₁ is null-measurable with finite measure, so (measure_diff) Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {β ≤ u}) = Lⁿ(Q₁) − F(β − 1) = 1 − F(β − 1) > 1/2 ≥ 1/2.

4. The bound |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u| (Simon (35)). Both functions below are integrable on Q₁.
 – β = 0. The claim is 0 ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|, which is true.
 – β > 0. For μ-a.e. y (namely y ∈ Q₁ ∖ Z) we have |u(y)| ≥ β·1_{β ≤ ũ}(y). Indeed, if β ≤ ũ(y) = u(y) then |u(y)| ≥ u(y) ≥ β, and otherwise |u(y)| ≥ 0. Integrating over Q₁ gives ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ β·Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {β ≤ ũ}) = β·Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {β ≤ u}) ≥ β/2, by 0(c) and step 3.
 – β < 0. Likewise |u(y)| ≥ −u(y) ≥ −β = |β| on Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β}. So ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ |β|·Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β}) ≥ |β|/2.
In every case |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|.

Steps 3 and 4 give the three conclusions for this β. ∎
key_steps: Lⁿ(Q₁) = 1 via the measure-preserving coordinate map; a Borel representative ũ makes the level sets of u null-measurable with the same measures.
F(b) = Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ b}) is nondecreasing with F → 1 at +∞ and F → 0 at −∞ (continuity of measure).
β := least integer with F(β) ≥ 1/2; integrality gives Q₁ ∩ {β ≤ u} = Q₁ ∖ {u ≤ β − 1}, of measure 1 − F(β − 1) > 1/2.
Integrating |u| ≥ |β| over the half-measure set {β ≤ u} (β > 0) or {u ≤ β} (β < 0) gives |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|.
